title: Girls Peter Pan Collar Dress Sewing Pattern – Free PDF

Garment Girls A-line dress with Peter Pan collar

Level Easy (confident beginner)

Sizes US 2 – 18 (height 91 – 165 cm)

Fabric Cotton poplin, lawn, chambray, gingham, light linen, fine corduroy

Pieces 6

This free girls Peter Pan collar dress sewing pattern is the kind of dress that never goes out of style: a simple A-line shape with no waist seam, short set-in sleeves and a soft rounded collar that frames her face. It closes with a row of twelve little buttons down the back, and the inside is neatly finished with a one-piece facing, so it feels as good as it looks.

Design details of the girls Peter Pan collar dress

The Girls Peter Pan Collar Dress is a classic little dress with a very simple construction: one front piece, two back pieces, two sleeves, a two-part collar and a neck facing. In our photo it is sewn in a washed dusty rose linen-cotton with a crisp white collar, but it looks just as sweet in a small gingham, a floral lawn or a fine needlecord for winter.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the only lines you sew are the shoulders, the armholes, the side seams and the neckline: there are no darts and no waist seam, the A-line shape does all the work. The collar is cut in two halves that meet at the centre front, which gives the little rounded notch you see under the chin. On the back, the vertical line is the centre back opening, with the buttons on the left back and the buttonholes on the right back. The two short lines near the neck are the shoulder darts, on sizes 7 to 18 only.

The neckline and the whole back opening are finished in one go with a one-piece facing, so there are no raw edges at the neck and no separate button bands to sew. A slightly crisp cotton or linen like the one in our photo keeps the collar flat and the A-line shape clean.

  • A-line (trapeze) shape with no waist seam, knee length on most sizes
  • Rounded Peter Pan collar in two halves, finished with a neck facing
  • Short set-in sleeves with a little ease at the cap
  • Full-length back opening with 12 buttons (1 cm)
  • One-piece front with no darts; small back shoulder darts on sizes 7–18
  • Clean inside: neck and back opening finished with one facing

The collar and the facing (steps 4 to 6 below) are the only parts that need a little patience. Everything else is straight seams and a simple hem, so this is a lovely dress for a confident beginner who wants to learn collars and buttonholes.

Sizing guide

Choose the size from the child’s chest measurement, not from her age: the dress is loose at the waist and hips. Between two sizes, choose the larger one. Not sure how to measure? Read how to take body measurements and how to choose your size.

Kids sizes: US 2 to 18, drafted for a height of 91 to 165 cm. US sizes are a guide only, always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished dress measurements

The finished chest has about 5 cm of ease, so the dress is comfortable without being baggy. Back length is measured at the centre back, from the neckline seam to the finished hem. Size 7 is drafted from a slimmer body chart than size 6: if the child measures between the two, compare the finished chest. Kids’ sizes vary between brands, so always measure.

Fabric amounts

Estimated by laying out every piece of each size without folding, with a small safety margin. Add extra to match checks or for one-way prints. For a contrast collar, a 30 cm piece of white cotton is plenty.

Common fit adjustments

Length. Each size is drafted for the height in the chart. To lengthen or shorten, add or remove the same amount at the hem of the Front, the Backs and the Back Neck Facings, keeping the A-line angle of the side seams.

Growing room. Because there is no waist seam, this dress grows well with the child: choose by chest, and if she is between sizes, take the larger one and hem it a little shorter for now.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 0.9 to 1.5 m (1 to 1 3/4 yd) of 150 cm wide light to medium woven fabric: cotton poplin or lawn, chambray, gingham, light linen or linen-cotton, fine needlecord
  • Collar (optional contrast): the same fabric, or a white cotton or small print
  • Light fusible interfacing: 0.5 m, for the facings and the upper collar
  • Buttons: 12 buttons, 1 cm (3/8″), all sizes
  • Matching all-purpose thread
  • Hand sewing needle, pins or clips and a point turner

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front: cut 1, single layer
  • 2 Back: cut 2 (one left, one right)
  • 3 Sleeve: cut 2 (mirror)
  • 4 Front Neck Facing: cut 1, single layer + interfacing
  • 5 Back Neck Facing: cut 2 (mirror) + interfacing
  • 6 Peter Pan Collar: cut 4 (2 left + 2 right), interface 2

The Front and the Front Neck Facing are drawn whole, with the centre front line in the middle: cut them from a single layer of fabric, right side up, not on the fold.

Choosing fabric for a Peter Pan collar dress

A Peter Pan collar looks best when it lies flat and keeps its round shape, so choose a light to medium woven fabric that presses well: cotton poplin, cotton lawn, chambray, gingham, light linen or a linen-cotton blend. For the colder months, a baby needlecord (fine corduroy), viyella or brushed cotton gives a cosy version to wear with tights.

The classic look is a white collar on a coloured or printed dress, like the one in our photo. Avoid stretch knits and very slippery fabrics for a first make: the collar and the buttonholes are much easier on a stable cotton. Pre-wash the fabric the way the dress will be washed, because children’s clothes go in the machine often. Our guide on how to use fusible interfacing helps you get a crisp collar.

Sewing notes

Fit & style

Easy A-line fit with about 5 cm of chest ease. Choose by chest; between sizes, take the larger one.

Fabrics

Light to medium wovens that press crisply. Avoid knits and slippery fabrics for a first make.

Cutting & sewing

Staystitch the necklines right after cutting and test one buttonhole on a scrap first.

Printable sewing tutorial

Need help completing the project?

Get the full printable tutorial for the Girls Peter Pan Collar Dress: detailed step-by-step sewing instructions with clear illustrations, a sizing guide, fabric amounts per size and the list of materials you need.

  • Illustrated diagrams for every step, from the collar and facing to the 12 buttonholes
  • Size charts in cm and inches, finished measurements and fabric amounts per size
  • Video guides for the key techniques, with links and QR codes
  • Printable PDF with A0 pattern files, instant download

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew with right sides together, finish the raw edges with a serger or a zigzag stitch and press every seam as you go. “Left” and “right” always mean as worn.

  1. Prepare the pieces. Fuse interfacing to the Front Neck Facing, both Back Neck Facings and two collar pieces (one left, one right). Staystitch the Front and Back necklines 7 mm from the edge, and finish the side seams of the dress and the underarm edges of the sleeves.
  2. Back shoulder darts. Sizes 7–18 only: fold each dart, stitch from the shoulder edge to the tip without backstitching, knot the threads and press toward the centre back.
  3. Shoulders. Sew the Front to the Backs at the shoulders, finish the allowances separately and press open.
  4. Make the collar. Pair each interfaced collar piece with a plain one and stitch the outer curve and short ends. Notch, trim to 5 mm, turn and press, rolling the seam slightly underneath. Baste both collars to the neckline, meeting at the centre front and stopping at the centre back notches.
  5. Prepare the facing. Join the Front Neck Facing to the two Back Neck Facings at the shoulders, press the seams open and finish the long outer edge all around.
  6. Facing: neckline and back opening. Lay the facing over the collar, right sides together, and stitch in one go from the hem mark up one back opening, around the neck and down the other side. Trim, clip, understitch, turn the facing inside and press.
  7. Side seams. Pin the Front to the Backs at the sides, matching the notches, stitch from the armhole to the hem and press open.
  8. Sleeves. Easestitch the cap, sew the underarm seam and hem the sleeve (5 mm + 1.5 cm). Set the sleeve into the armhole, matching the shoulder notch, spread the ease evenly and stitch.
  9. Hem. Turn up the 2 cm hem (5 mm, then 1.5 cm), easing the curve, fold the ends of the facing under in line with the hem and stitch. Slipstitch the facing ends by hand.
  10. Buttonholes and buttons. Make 12 horizontal 1.2 cm buttonholes on the right back, then sew the buttons on the left back centre line. Give the dress a final press, the collar from the under side. Need help? See how to sew buttonholes and buttons.

Tips and common mistakes

Collar edge that shows the seam. Press the collar from the under side and roll the seam a few millimetres toward the under collar, so only the top fabric shows.

Collar halves that do not meet. Baste the collars to the neckline first and check from the right side that the two front ends touch exactly at the centre front before you sew the facing.

Facing that rolls to the outside. Understitch as far around the neckline as you can, and tack the facing to the shoulder seam allowances by hand.

Uneven buttonholes. Test one buttonhole on a scrap with the same layers of fabric and interfacing, and mark all twelve with chalk before you start.

How to style the girls Peter Pan collar dress

Classic: a white contrast collar on a gingham or a small floral print, with white socks and ballet flats.

Winter: in fine corduroy with tights, a cardigan and ankle boots.

Party: mother-of-pearl or fabric-covered buttons make the back the star of the dress.

Looking for more dresses for her? Sew our girls twirl dress sewing pattern with a full circle skirt, or the girls puff sleeve dress sewing pattern in the same size range.

Care

Wash at 30 °C inside out with similar colours, buttons done up. Press the collar from the under side with a little steam.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every edge, plus a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the dress and on the sleeves.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download comes in A4 and US Letter, as a printable PDF with one file per size, US 2 to 18.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by the child’s chest measurement. Between two sizes, choose the larger one and adjust the length at the hem.

Is this dress good for beginners?

Yes, for a confident beginner. The collar and facing need care and the buttonholes need a little practice; the paid tutorial has illustrations and video guides for both.

How many buttons do I need?

Twelve buttons of 1 cm (3/8″) for every size. Flat buttons are the most comfortable at the back.

Can I make the collar in a different fabric?

Yes. A white cotton or a small print gives the classic look. Use a fabric of a similar weight so the collar lies flat.

Can I use a stretch fabric?

It is designed for woven fabrics, so no stretch is needed. A knit would make the collar and the buttonholes wavy.

Does the dress need a lining?

No, it is unlined: the neckline and the back opening are finished with a facing. With a very light fabric, choose a slightly denser weave.

How long does it take to sew?

About 4 to 5 hours for a confident beginner, including the twelve buttonholes.
